proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On the fixed known support \(H\) defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, along sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), along which \(R(P)\to0\)? proposed_statement_changes.reason: The corrected frontier definition makes \(R(P)\) available only when \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). The current question quantifies over all of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), including laws at which \(R(P)\) is undefined. Explicit compatibility is the minimal domain restriction and is also needed by the established upper-endpoint theorem.

proposed.name: fixed-support minimax transition handle
proposed.construction: Within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), the support is the fixed known rectangle union \(H\) and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on \(H\), so a shrinking conditional-support hole is not an admissible path. Study minimax excess-endpoint risk along fixed-support sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), along which \(R(P)\to0\), by constructing and verifying Le Cam two-point or Assouad families of \(\beta\)-H\"older perturbations of \(g\) and/or \(\nu_P\) that preserve every class restriction and compatibility and separate the optimized endpoints of \(\Theta(P)\). A support-topology transition must instead be posed on a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class with explicit geometry and density conditions. This handle asserts no lower bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle must respect the corrected domain of \(R(P)\) and the compatibility restriction already required by the established uniform upper bound. This adds no lower-bound premise and leaves the least-favorable-family construction open.

proposed.statement: On the fixed known support \(H\) defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, along sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), along which \(R(P)\to0\)? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of estimating the obstacle boundary from the cost of estimating the signed objective? A shrinking support-hole transition lies outside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
proposed.justification: The upper rate becomes economically interpretable only after determining whether its obstacle and signed-objective terms are unavoidable along compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\).
proposed.gap: The known fixed rectangle support and uniform positive density lower bound exclude a shrinking support-hole transition from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Existing results provide neither a matching fixed-support lower bound over compatible laws nor a separately formalized varying-support class.
proposed.consumer: A matching fixed-support lower bound would show whether shorter uniformly honest sensitivity intervals require stronger functional restrictions or merely a better estimator; a support-topology claim must await a distinct class.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching minimax lower bound, uniform along fixed-support sequences in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\) and \(R(P)\to0\), that separately attributes endpoint loss to estimating the obstacle boundary and to estimating the signed objective; any support-topology transition additionally requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
obligation.obstruction: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is the same known finite rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) throughout \(H\). Hence the suggested shrinking-hole family is outside the frozen class. Within fixed \(H\), the primitives establish the upper bound but supply no verified two-point or hypercube family that simultaneously remains in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), preserves \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), has bounded product-experiment divergence, and separates an optimized WAOSS endpoint at the asserted rate.
obligation.attempted: The natural route perturbs \(g\) by a local \(\beta\)-H\"older bump and perturbs \(\nu_P\) to isolate the two error sources. A shrinking hole violates fixed support; on fixed support, verifying the density and outcome bounds, obstacle compatibility, divergence bound, and optimized-endpoint separation is precisely the missing least-favorable-family construction. Assuming those properties would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: The established theorem gives the uniform upper endpoint error \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\) over laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Also, \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is fixed and known and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on all of \(H\), so support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Thus the current minimax problem can let \(R(P)\to0\) only along compatible laws on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole lower bound belongs to a new varying-support class. No matching fixed-support lower bound or decomposition into obstacle and signed-objective costs follows from the frozen primitives.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The same-bundle claim narrowing introduces the free symbol \(\mathcal C_P\) and requires the statement metadata and recorded obligation to use the corrected compatibility domain.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula; the regular witness shows that this singleton is not identified over that published class.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design.

Inference based on conditional moment inequalities supplies a general testing and confidence-set framework, not the necessary-and-sufficient support-local obstacle certificate for this WAOSS completion class.
Sharp identification regions under convex moment predictions supply general convex identified-region logic, not this continuum-to-mesh clipping and Hausdorff certificate.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set in nonparametric instrumental-variable models; this is not a WAOSS obstacle or endpoint result.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimators admit uniform Gaussian approximations and confidence bands.
Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes; it does not characterize this partially identified WAOSS sensitivity frontier.

prose_updates.tldr: Marginal quasi-stayers do not identify the weighted WAOSS singleton claimed by de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): at a regular heterogeneous-baseline witness, the published completion class contains an affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is all of \(\mathbb R\). The positive result is instead a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure. Its completion class adds a finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, a continuous support version of \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline conditional-mean identity with a continuous baseline trend; the affine lifts satisfy both trend clauses. Marginal quasi-stayers are not required for this characterization, and its finite attained obstacle interval does not transfer to the unrestricted source class. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton formula; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 remains an analogous result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The finite outer program yields a uniformly honest interval on the fixed-support regular subclass, while minimaxity along compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\) remains open.

project_justification.gap: The proceedings paper states weighted WAOSS point identification under Assumptions 1--4, but marginal quasi-stayers do not imply the baseline-conditional positivity invoked immediately before display (4) of its Appendix proof. The regular witness gives a generic-class certificate of failure: the published completion class admits a legal affine recession ray whose WAOSS image is \(\mathbb R\). The source's per-dose parallel-trends clause also does not by itself justify substituting the random diagonal dose; the sensitivity model therefore retains that per-dose clause and separately imposes the realized-baseline identity \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)\), with \(m_Q\) a continuous version of the corresponding conditional mean given \(X\).
project_justification.niche: The paper separates three objects that cannot be conflated: the unrestricted published class, which is unbounded at the witness; a bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class with continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel trends, and a separate realized-baseline identity, which has an exact finite obstacle interval; and the baseline-conditional zero-support regime, in which that interval collapses to the published weighted formula. On source-admissible observed laws, only source completions also satisfying the added sensitivity restrictions are characterized; no global class equality or inclusion is asserted.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the source-class recession-ray counterexample and then characterizes the strengthened sensitivity class by a full-observed-law affine lift that satisfies both trend clauses, attained interval geometry, the exact criterion \(R(P)=0\) on the compatible domain, conditional-support singleton recovery, obstacle compatibility and constant-one clipping, certified finite programs, and uniform outer coverage on a fixed rectangle-support subclass. The common-zero-baseline scalar interval from arXiv:2405.04465v4 is retained solely as prior-art validation, and the source paper's separate parametric estimator is outside the challenge.

sampling_model.units: Each superpopulation unit has observed \(Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2\) and one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\). The sensitivity class retains the source's per-dose conditional-parallel-trends equality and separately requires \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m_Q(X)\) almost surely, where \(m_Q\) is an explicitly chosen continuous version of \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X]\). Realized-diagonal and period-two causal-movement integrability are imposed explicitly. The affine lifts satisfy the per-dose and realized-baseline clauses simultaneously.
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline and follow-up doses are continuous and exact stayers are excluded. The sensitivity sharpness theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the support version \(g\), and the separate realized-baseline identity in addition to the source's per-dose parallel trends. On an observed law satisfying the source assumptions, the reported finite interval concerns only completions satisfying these additional restrictions and does not transfer upward to the unrestricted source class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is combined with the signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program. The event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) yields uniform outer coverage and the proved excess-endpoint rate. A matching lower bound remains open for compatible fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\); shrinking support holes require a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.

prose_updates.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix argument immediately before display (4)) state a weighted WAOSS singleton under marginal quasi-stayers, although the proof invokes baseline-conditional positivity. The accepted source-class recession-ray proposition shows that the issue is substantive: at the regular witness the published completion class generates every value in \(\mathbb R\). Only this non-representability result transfers directly to that class. The positive finite interval is a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure; it adds a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline identity with a continuous \(m_Q\). The affine lifts satisfy both trend clauses. Under baseline-conditional zero support the interval collapses to the proceedings paper's weighted formula. Section 4.1, Assumption 5, and Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 provide an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval of de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, arXiv:2405.04465v4, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2) is prior art used only as an algebraic sanity check. Andrews and Shi (2013) provide general conditional-moment-inequality inference, rather than the necessary-and-sufficient support-local obstacle certificate proved here. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011) develop convex sharp-region logic; Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) optimize weighted functionals under convex restrictions; and Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) obtain linear-program bounds on finite discrete support. Voronin (2025) studies values of programs that are already finite. None of those results supplies the exact clipping and Hausdorff certificate taking this continuum WAOSS class to a mesh. Freyberger (2017) studies completeness and consistency in nonparametric instrumental-variable models and data-driven bounds on identified-set diameter, not support-local WAOSS obstacles or endpoint inference. Sasaki and Ura (2025) develop bias correction and limit theory for point-identified slow-mover panel estimands, not this partially identified completion frontier. For inference, Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) establish uniform calibrated projection for finite moment systems, Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015) give uniform series-regression theory, and Cattaneo, Chandak, Jansson, and Ma (2024) give support-edge-adaptive conditional-density inference. The inference theorem makes no general advance in those component theories: for this WAOSS model it narrowly composes a primitive support-edge cell-mean band, a signed-measure band, the certified continuum discretization, a denominator band, and measurable ratio optimization. The proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated, and no current result supplies the open fixed-support minimax lower bound over compatible laws.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive identified set is exact only for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class, which retains the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition and separately imposes a realized-baseline identity with a continuous conditional-mean version. The inference theorem additionally fixes a known finite rectangle union, \(\beta\), a uniform positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation, and uses a conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed-measure control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation without density smoothness, strict feasibility, or optimizer uniqueness. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). A matching lower bound as \(R(P)\to0\) along compatible laws on fixed \(H\) remains open; shrinking-hole asymptotics require a new varying-support class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The negative conclusion is exact for the published class at the regular witness: its legal affine recession ray generates all of \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The finite set \(\Theta(P)\) is instead the sharp causal set for a strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class with a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), the source's per-dose parallel-trends condition, and a separate realized-baseline identity with a continuous \(m_Q\); the affine lifts satisfy both clauses. Marginal quasi-stayers are unnecessary for that sensitivity characterization. No global equality or inclusion with the source class is claimed, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 concerns unweighted \(\delta_1\); and the common-zero-baseline scalar bounds in arXiv:2405.04465v4 are prior art. The source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged. Uniform outer inference is confined to the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, density-bounded-below, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. No lower-bound optimality result is claimed; support-topology asymptotics, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length are also outside scope.
